headline: Everything
at a glance.
sub: The house, the sky, the day — on one screen.
body: Weather, clocks, countdowns, thermostats, room temperatures, your Mac’s vitals. Panels refresh themselves and keep refreshing while the board is up.
howto: Tap + to add a panel, then pick what it shows
Drag a panel to move it, pull its corner to resize

headline: A board for
each part
of your life.
sub: Keep as many as you like. Switch in a tap.
body: School on one, the house on another, your servers on a third. Every board syncs over your private iCloud, so the one you build on the Mac is already on the phone.
howto: Tap the back arrow for the list of boards
Long-press a board to rename, duplicate or delete

headline: Nine themes.
Six wallpapers.
sub: Set the whole board, or one panel at a time.
body: A theme decides background, panel fill, border and type colour together. Any single panel can break ranks — go frosted, transparent, or paint its own gradient.
howto: Tap the palette to open Board Appearance
Pick a theme, add a wallpaper, then set the scrim

headline: One picture,
cut across
the board.
sub: Panels that show their own slice of the wallpaper.
body: Set a panel to Board Image and it masks the board’s backdrop in place, lined up with its neighbours. Move it and the picture re-cuts. Frost the rest and the whole thing reads as glass.
howto: Panel › Appearance › Background › Board Image
Raise the scrim until the numbers read clearly

headline: Your Mac,
on your
phone.
sub: CPU, memory, disk and network, live.
body: The Mac app publishes its own vitals over your local network — no account, no server in the middle. Twelve chart styles and seven progress meters to draw them with.
howto: Open Status Board on the Mac to start the bridge
The phone finds it on the network by itself

headline: Built from
28 kinds
of panel.
sub: Clocks, feeds, graphs, tables, web clips and more.
body: Weather, calendar, health, GitHub, App Store Connect, Home Assistant, Nest, HomeKit, Tesla, Canvas grades and schedules — or any JSON URL you point it at.
howto: Tap + › choose a kind › fill in the source
Set a refresh interval per panel, from seconds to hours

headline: Change the
whole board
in two taps.
sub: Theme, wallpaper, base colour, gradient, scrim.
body: Board Appearance sets the look of everything at once, and “Apply to panels” decides whether panels follow along. Any panel that has chosen a theme of its own always keeps it.
howto: Tap the palette in the toolbar
Pick a theme, then add a wallpaper underneath

headline: The whole wall,
on one screen.
sub: A grid you arrange yourself, at any size.
body: Drop panels onto the grid, drag them where you want them, and let the board fill the display. Leave the iPad on a stand and it keeps itself up to date all day.
howto: Drag a panel to move it; drag its corner to resize
Pinch the grid to add rows and columns

headline: Alternate
dashboards,
one tap apart.
sub: The sidebar holds every board you have made.
body: Grades, today’s classes and what is still owed on one board; the house on the next. Rename, duplicate or delete from the same list, and iCloud carries the change everywhere.
howto: Tap a board in the sidebar to switch to it
Command-N makes a new one; the + menu has starter boards

headline: Every panel,
editable
in place.
sub: Kind, source, refresh, renderer, colour.
body: Open a panel and change what it reads, how often, and how it draws. Chart style, progress format, accent colour and background are all per panel — nothing is baked into the theme.
howto: Tap a panel to select it, then tap Edit
Command-D duplicates; Shift-Command-C and Shift-Command-V copy between boards

headline: Lay out every
screen its
own way.
sub: One board. A different arrangement per device.
body: A Mac has room for fourteen panels; a watch has room for one. Give each device class its own layout — and preview it at that device’s real point size before you ever look at the hardware.
howto: Shift-Command-D opens the device preview
Pick Mac, iPad, iPhone, TV or Watch and rearrange

headline: Nine themes,
and room
to disagree.
sub: Status Board, Glass, Carbon, Slate, Paper, Terminal, Blueprint, Sunset, Aurora.
body: Pick one for the board and it sets everything at once. Then override any panel that wants to stand out — or turn the theme off and choose every colour yourself.
howto: Board Appearance sets the theme, wallpaper and scrim
Panel › Appearance overrides just that panel

headline: Frosted,
masked,
or invisible.
sub: Backgrounds that do more than sit behind the numbers.
body: Solid, gradient, image, blur, transparent — or Board Image, where each panel shows its own aligned slice of one wallpaper and the gaps between panels cut into the picture.
howto: Set the board wallpaper first, then the panel style
Blur and scrim keep text legible over a busy image

headline: Build the board.
Put it everywhere.
sub: The Mac is where boards are made.
body: Lay panels out on a grid, point them at whatever you want to watch, and the same board appears on your iPhone, iPad, Apple TV and Watch through your own private iCloud.
howto: Command-N for a new board, + for a panel
Command-Z and Shift-Command-Z undo and redo every edit

headline: Alternate
dashboards.
sub: As many boards as you have things to watch.
body: Keep the house on one, school on another, your build servers on a third. The sidebar switches between them; Spotlight finds them by name, and Handoff picks one up on the next device.
howto: The + menu ships starter boards to build from
Right-click a board to rename, duplicate or delete

headline: Edit in place.
Every panel,
every pixel.
sub: 28 panel kinds, 12 chart styles, 7 progress meters.
body: Turn on Edit and every panel grows handles: drag to move, pull the corner to resize, hit the dial to change what it reads and how it draws. Command-Z undoes any of it.
howto: Command-E toggles Edit; the toolbar has it too
Alert above / below turns any number into a notification

headline: One picture,
cut across
the board.
sub: Panels that show their own slice of the wallpaper.
body: Set a panel to Board Image and it masks the board’s backdrop in place, lined up with its neighbours. Move it and the picture re-cuts. Frost the rest and the whole thing reads as glass.
howto: Panel › Appearance › Background › Board Image
Raise the scrim until the numbers read clearly

headline: Nine themes.
Or none at all.
sub: Status Board, Glass, Carbon, Slate, Paper, Terminal, Blueprint, Sunset, Aurora.
body: Every theme sets background, panel fill, border and type together, light or dark. Add one of six wallpapers underneath, then dial the scrim until the numbers read the way you want.
howto: Board Appearance is in the toolbar and the Board menu
Custom lets you set every colour by hand

headline: Your Mac,
on every
other screen.
sub: CPU, memory, disk, network and uptime, published live.
body: The Mac app runs a small bridge on your own network and offers itself over Bonjour. The Apple TV and the iPhone find it by themselves. Nothing leaves the house, and there is no account to make.
howto: Nothing to set up — open the Mac app and it publishes
The sbctl tool pushes your own values onto any panel

headline: The big screen,
finally useful.
sub: Your board, full size, all day.
body: Weather, the house, the schedule and your Mac’s vitals on the television nobody is watching. Boards arrive from iCloud — the Apple TV displays them, so there is nothing to set up on it.
howto: Sign in to the same iCloud account and wait a moment
Boards you make on the Mac appear here by themselves

headline: Pick a board,
or cycle them all.
sub: Pin one to this TV, or let it rotate.
body: Choose which board this Apple TV shows and it stays chosen — even after the board arrives again from another device. Or set an interval and let it move through every board on its own.
howto: Press Menu for the board list and settings
Auto-cycle rotates boards on a timer you choose

headline: Nine themes,
made for a room.
sub: Bright enough to read from the sofa.
body: Each theme sets the whole board together, and the TV layout respects the title-safe area so nothing important sits under the bezel. Turn that off when the screen has no overscan to fight.
howto: Set the theme on the Mac; the TV picks it up
Fill Screen in TV settings uses the full panel edge to edge

headline: A wallpaper
worth leaving on.
sub: Frosted panels over one moving picture.
body: Aurora, Dusk, Grid, Starfield, Topography and Halftone animate quietly behind the board. Panels can frost over them or cut their own slice out of them — on a 4K screen the difference shows.
howto: Board Appearance › Wallpaper, then set Animates
Reduce Motion is honoured; the picture holds still

headline: Watch the build
from the sofa.
sub: The Mac bridge reaches the television too.
body: CPU, memory, disk and network stream from the Mac over your own network. The Mac also renders web pages offscreen and sends them across, so a web clip works on a TV that has no browser.
howto: Open Status Board on the Mac; the TV finds it
Web-clip panels are rendered by the Mac and relayed

headline: On your
wrist.
sub: The same board, one panel at a time.

headline: Tap for
the detail.
sub: Full screen, full size, no squinting.

headline: Every board
you own.
sub: Arrives from iCloud. Nothing to set up.

headline: 28 kinds of panel,
on a 4K screen.
sub: Clocks, weather, graphs, tables, feeds, web clips.
body: Everything the Mac and iPhone can show, the television shows too — including web pages, which the Mac renders offscreen and relays, so a panel of live web content works on a device with no browser at all.
howto: Build the board anywhere; the TV just displays it
Auto-cycle moves through your boards on a timer
